precisionProbes.finding: narrow one-site reading of C2' (per-entry loop over ptrlog[0] only); f2 stays RED because the presence/count rules independently refuse the deleted pointerdown. Demonstrates the frozen one-line wording does not realise the stated f2-green without also making the press presence optional.
one-site reading of C3' (relax the numeric pointerId rule only); f3 stays RED on pointer-order-wrong via the release-id equality. The KILL needs the equality relaxed too.

one-site reading of C5' (remove the additive pointer-nonce-wrong check only); f5 stays RED on plain-trace-wrong plus the r61-path nonce-not-invocation-bound rule. The KILL needs the carried prefix rule and the r61 typed-trace rule dropped too.

instrumentFindings.finding: 'check only the first pointer entry' is not realised by the narrow per-entry-loop edit: measured probe f2 stays exit 1 with pointer-order-wrong x2 (P-C2-narrow sha b74393c099880ab9...). The frozen kill rule needs the composed defect (per-entry ptrlog[0] only + missing-press tolerated + first-pairing-only), which greens f2 and is KILLED at mutant 34f29a5806c8ea7d....

f3 (pointerId deleted from the pointerdown) is refused TWICE: the numeric-type rule (pointer-id-wrong) and the release-id equality (pointer-order-wrong). Relaxing only the type rule leaves f3 red (P-C3-typeonly sha 1fd873a861114856...). The KILL requires both sites (mutant a79790245fa9c867...).

f5 (corrupted final valueAfter) is refused THREE times on this generation: additive pointer-nonce-wrong (plainTrace rederivation), carried plain-trace-wrong (prefix binding), and the r61-path nonce-not-invocation-bound (exact-nonce-in-typed-trace). Removing only the additive check leaves f5 red (P-C5-additiveonly sha 2d3902f5996a2537...). The KILL requires all three plus the r61 valueAfterTyping equality (mutant 96dcb93124aecc7b..., 4 sites). Exec3's report disclosed the carried-rule part in advance; the r61-path rule appeared with the later revision and is measured here.

Scoring probes needs `--shot <fixtures>` plus the two shotFiles overrides (r61-a-pointer-press.png, r61-b-typed.png) because the receipt's steps name a-pointer-press.png/b-typed.png while the fixture dir stores r61-*-prefixed copies. Without the overrides the receipt and every probe carry 2 png-missing findings and no mutant could ever green a probe (measured). The frozen live command uses corpus/evidence/round61/chromium-pointer-domain PNGs whose names match the live receipt, so live scoring is unaffected; any replay from measure/ must pass the overrides.

The green baseline is Exec2's real runner smoke receipt (smoke-r61b sha 7839c0a6..., copied to r61-base-receipt.json), so the pointer records are live-delivery bytes; it is still a smoke receipt, and the committed corpus receipt plus the closure proof remain data-pass obligations. This seat ran no browser.

The selftest case r61-f2-pointerdown-deleted derives its forgery with an ARRAY-KEY delete (ptrlog.1 delete => a hole, length 3), which the counter refuses as pointer-log-wrong + pointer-order-wrong; the frozen probe f2 deletes the element (Python del => length 2), refused as pointer-order-wrong x2. The selftest case and the frozen probe therefore exercise different bytes; both are refused by the pristine counter, and the C2' mutant greens the probe while the selftest case (hole shape) still fails. Recorded so the L1 does not conflate them.

f1-f4 edit only ptrlog; f5 edits only the last plainTrace valueAfter. They never touch mouselog or journey, which is coherent with the counter's independent seq/journey rules; it is precisely why the composed C2' can green f2 while the r61-journey checks stay satisfied.
